citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The licensee is not using appropriate methods to prevent, control, diagnose, and treat disease and injuries. When
inspectors questioned the licensee about how castrations are performed for sugar gliders, she stated that she performs
castrations when requested. The procedure is not described in the Program of Veterinary Care, and the licensee has not
discussed it with her current attending veterinarian. The licensee manually restrains the animals for the procedure and
does not use anesthesia or analgesics.
Performing surgical procedures without anesthesia or analgesia causes unnecessary distress and pain on the animals
and is not considered adequate veterinary care.
Dealers must establish and maintain programs of adequate veterinary care that include the use of appropriate methods to
prevent, control, diagnose, and treat diseases and injuries. The licensee must discontinue these procedures immediately
and must use the attending veterinarian whenever such a procedure is necessary.

citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
During the inspection, inspectors found a common marmoset in the Breeder Room with shortened tail with fur loss over its
tail. The facility representative stated that the animal had self mutilated and been involved in fighting with other
marmosets but had not been seen by the veterinarian. Inspectors also identified a common marmoset in a different
enclosure in the Breeder Room with heavily matted fur and thinning fur on its tail; this animal also had not been seen by a
veterinarian.
In the Warm Room, inspectors found four dead Woodland Dormice in three different enclosures along with living Dormice.
In one of these cages, the dead animal was a pup, and the adult in the cage was extremely lethargic. The licensee
reported that she found a dead pup in that cage the day before, but did not notify the veterinarian. One of the dead
Dormice had matted blood and bedding on its underside, and another was dry and shrunken, indicating it had likely been
deceased for more than a day. Facility personnel did not identify these animals before the inspection.
Failing to conduct adequate daily observations to assess the animals’ health and well being and to maintain direct and
frequent communication with the attending veterinarian, can delay treatment and allow conditions to worsen.
Each dealer must establish and maintain programs of adequate veterinary care that include daily observation of all
animals and a mechanism for direct and frequent communication to ensure timely and accurate reporting of animal health,
behavior, and well being concerns to the attending veterinarian.
The licensee corrected these issues by taking the animals to the veterinarian during the inspection.

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
Multiple items in the marmoset and tamarin primary enclosures in the Breeder Room need cleaning or replacement.
These items include the PVC ladders, cage bedding, and cloth hammocks. Inspectors noted that these items were
excessively dirty in multiple enclosures, and brown smeared residue was present on the PVC items and cloth hammocks.
Regularly cleaning these items prevents excessive waste buildup, keeps the nonhuman primates from becoming soiled,
and reduces disease hazards, insects, pests, and odors.
The licensee must spot clean hard surfaces daily, and they must keep perches and shelves clean and replace them when
worn. Correct by 9/17/26.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representatives.
Additional Inspectors:
Louis Divincenti n
